name: demo_brightmart
text: Thanks for making the time, Priya. Before I show you anything, can you tell me what is going on at the stores right now? What made you take this meeting? Honestly, it's the stock-outs. Our billing system and our inventory don't talk to each other. Every week at least ten stores run out of fast-moving items, and we only find out when customers complain. Ten stores a week. What does a stock-out cost you, roughly, when it happens? Our finance team estimated around four lakh rupees a month in lost sales across the chain. And the store managers spend their Sunday doing manual counts. That's painful. How are you tracking inventory today? Excel sheets that the managers email to the head office every evening. And our accounts run on Tally. Got it. If you could fix one thing in the next quarter, what would it be? Real-time stock visibility, and automatic reorder alerts before we run out. That is exactly what our inventory module does. The billing counter updates stock the moment an item is sold, and when an item falls below a level you set, the store manager and the buyer both get an alert on their phone. That sounds good. But how long does it take to set up? We cannot shut stores down. We roll out store by store, usually overnight. A forty-store chain typically goes live in about six weeks. Six weeks is fine. What about Tally? We are not changing our accounting. You don't have to. We have a Tally connector that syncs sales and purchase entries every hour. Okay. To be very honest, we also met Zoho last week, and their quote was lower than what I expect from you. That's fair, and I'd rather you compare properly. Can I ask what was in their quote? Did it include the hardware and the store rollout? I think it was software only. Hardware was separate. Ours includes the billing hardware, the rollout team and the first year of support. If I put both side by side for forty stores, would that help you? Yes, that would help. What would forty stores cost with you? For forty stores, it comes to around twelve thousand rupees per store per month, so roughly four lakh eighty thousand a month. Hmm. That is close to what we lose from stock-outs. I'm not sure the CFO will see it that way. Who else is involved in this decision, besides you and the CFO? Our CFO, Mr. Rao, signs off on anything above two lakh a month. And the IT head will want to check the Tally integration. Would it make sense to set up a short session with Mr. Rao and the IT head, where we walk through the return on investment and the integration? Yes. Mr. Rao is free next Thursday. We want to decide before the new financial year in April. Perfect. I'll send you the side by side comparison and a pilot proposal for five stores by Monday, and we can meet Mr. Rao on Thursday. A pilot for five stores is a good idea. Send it to me and I will forward it to him. Great. Thank you, Priya. I'll also include the case study from FreshCart, they had the same stock-out problem. Thank you, Arjun. See you Thursday.
